clue.text: Revelling overhead?

definitions.note: adverb for the phrase meaning up on the roof

blocks.note: first meaning: out partying, the idiom used of cats and people out all night
second meaning, taken literally: up on the roof among the slates

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: a night out on the town and a perch up on the roof share one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a wild night out also literally describes being up on a roof, among its slates.

clue.text: Very rich and very drunk, which is not to be sniffed at

definitions.note: the word is the intensifier in the phrase for very rich

blocks.note: first meaning: the slang intensifier used in a phrase for enormous wealth
second meaning: slang for heavily intoxicated

blocks.clueFragment: which is not to be sniffed at
blocks.note: surface padding: a joke on the word's literal sense of smelling foul

explanation.surface: Someone wealthy and plastered is still worth knowing, so not to be sniffed at.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'which is not to be sniffed at' is a joke on the word's literal sense of smelling foul, which nobody would want to sniff.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word both for extreme wealth (in 'stinking rich') and for severe intoxication; literally it means foul-smelling.

clue.text: The front was where it should be: insert egg for bandy

definitions.text: The front was where it should be
definitions.note: a cricketing description of a fair dismissal

indicators.note: putting a word in to make the bandy word means the answer is that longer word with the inserted word taken out again

blocks.note: bandy legs curve outwards, so bandy means bow-legged
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction, perhaps from a cook or a tailor, about setting something right at the front and adding an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add EGG to the answer and you get BOWLEGGED, meaning bandy. The definition refers to a bowler's front foot being behind the crease, so it was no no-ball and the dismissal stands.
explanation.definitionFit: If the bowler's front foot lands legally the delivery is fair, so a batsman whose stumps are hit is out in the usual cricket way.

clue.text: Child of the South makes an uncontrolled movement

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A youngster from the southern states loses their footing.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a vehicle or person sliding out of control, so the verb means slides helplessly.

clue.text: Small-minded character without the right to good looks

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the character wraps around the right

blocks.note: a petty, small-minded nature
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited person with no claim to being attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Prettiness is the quality of being attractive in a delicate way, a kind of handsome appearance.

clue.text: A tinker's cursed in former Bantustan

indicators.note: something cursed is blighted and put out of its proper order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: An itinerant tinker swears his way through a South African homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bantustan was a nominally self-governing black homeland in apartheid South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Transkei was one of the homelands set up under apartheid South Africa, declared independent in 1976 and reabsorbed in 1994.

clue.text: Neither 3, 21 down, 16, 23 across, nor 11 8 etc - I won't sell you a ticket

definitions.text: I won't sell you a ticket
definitions.note: read as a respaced phrase saying the speaker is no tout

blocks.note: first meaning: a batsman not dismissed by any of the listed methods

blocks.clueFragment: I won't sell you a ticket
blocks.note: second meaning: respaced, the words say '...', and a tout sells tickets at inflated prices

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are the ways a batsman can be dismissed: bowled, caught, leg before wicket, stumped, handled the ball. Moving the word space gives NO TOUT, a tout being a ticket scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who escapes every mode of dismissal remains in, the scorecard's term for still batting at the end.

clue.text: See 11
A link man practising 14 across?

definitions.note: describes a person, the definition being cryptic

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who builds and uses contacts
second meaning, split as two words: a player working at the practice nets

explanation.walkthrough: Cricketers practise batting and bowling in 'the nets', so a player there is literally a net worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cultivates professional contacts is said to be networking, and practice at cricket happens inside netted enclosures.

clue.text: Girl painter holding carrier

indicators.note: the painter grips the carrier, so it sits within

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, a painter
a hod is a builder's tray for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A young woman artist carrying something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female given name, so it can stand for any girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: Operative was first to dance, a touch illegally?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of the dismissal

blocks.note: a hand is a worker, an operative
led means was in front
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A worker who opened the dancing and perhaps groped someone improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: Handled the ball was a way for a batsman to be given out in cricket for touching the ball with a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching the ball with the hand while batting, without permission, was an illegal act in cricket and led to dismissal.

clue.text: Time for the news - I left wrapping the food

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the material used to wrap food

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
info is information, the news
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: It is time for the news, so I go off, wrapping up the meal first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrapping' looks like a container instruction but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet is used in kitchens to cover dishes and parcel up sandwiches.

clue.text: Riding 20 for appeal after appeal

definitions.note: a riding is literally one third of Yorkshire
short for the official consulted on referral

blocks.note: first meaning: the three Ridings of Yorkshire were its ..., the word coming from Old Norse for ... part
second meaning: the TV official in cricket reviews an appeal after the on-field call

explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, an English county, was divided into three Ridings. Cricket's TV umpire, called the third umpire, decides referrals after a players' appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding originally meant a third part of a county, and the replay official in cricket is called the third umpire.

clue.text: Tree surgery follows a spasm, 1 of 11

indicators.note: surgery cuts and reworks, so these letters are operated on and rearranged
says the reworked tree comes after the spasm in the answer

blocks.note: a crick is a painful muscle spasm, as in the neck
the letters of tree rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon's work after suffering a muscle spasm.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 of 11' is a member of an eleven, the size of a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side fields eleven players, so a player is one of that eleven.

clue.text: China's royal race

blocks.note: the crown stands for royalty
the Derby is the famous flat horse race at Epsom

explanation.surface: A country has a royal horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: China here is porcelain, not the country; Crown Derby is a make of English porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown Derby is fine porcelain made in the English city of Derby, and porcelain is called china.

clue.text: Dress again with herb: OAPs 23 down, more often 22 down, 7 permanently

definitions.text: OAPs 23 down, more often 22 down, 7 permanently
definitions.note: a cryptic description, read as pensioners who are unwell and a batsman leaving the field

blocks.note: re-tire, tire being an old word for attire
dill is a herb

explanation.surface: A recipe line about re-dressing a dish with herbs, followed by notes on pensioners' health.
explanation.walkthrough: OAPs (old-age pensioners) are retired, and 23 down is SICK, so ill. A batsman more often 'retires hurt' (22 down), and one who leaves through illness is recorded as not out (7) for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensioners who are sick are literally retired and unwell, and a batsman leaving the field through sickness is recorded with this scorebook phrase.

clue.text: Walker at the gate to grow feeble changing 14 across's heart

definitions.note: a cryptic reading of the phrase word by word

indicators.note: changing says the letters of the phrase before it are rearranged
the heart of a word is its middle, so its outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: the ten letters of these two words rearranged
the cross-referenced word without its first two and last two letters

explanation.surface: A pedestrian standing at a gate starts to weaken, changing their heart about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: a leg is a walker, before means at or in front of, and a wicket is a small gate. 14 across is CRICKETER, whose centre is ICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg is the limb used for walking, before means in front of, and wicket is an old word for a small gate.

clue.text: Directions in the course of being permanent

blocks.note: E and N, the compass abbreviations for east and north
during means in the course of

explanation.surface: Instructions given while something is made permanent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting goes on and on through time, which is what a long-standing or permanent thing does.

clue.text: £1,000 for a way to be 21 down breaking stones

blocks.note: K, for kilo, is a thousand, slang for a thousand pounds
to be caught napping is to be taken unawares

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds as one way to be trapped, while labouring at stone-breaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is CAUGHT, and 'caught napping' is the idiom for being found off guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Knapping is the craft of striking flint or stone to split and shape it, as for tools or building.

clue.text: Ventures into water to see how the land lies?

definitions.note: plural noun: depth measurements taken in water

definitions.text: to see how the land lies
definitions.note: the word names probes made for this purpose

blocks.note: first meaning: measurements of depth taken by lowering a line into the sea

blocks.clueFragment: to see how the land lies
blocks.note: second meaning: tentative enquiries to discover opinion, the figurative use

explanation.walkthrough: 'How the land lies' is literal for a sailor checking the seabed and figurative for someone testing opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors measure depth by lowering a weighted line, and the same word covers cautious enquiries into others' views.

clue.text: He won't raise a finger if you're 7

definitions.text: He won't raise a finger if you're 7

blocks.note: surface reading: someone idle who will not help
setter's reading: 7 is NOT OUT, and in cricket the official signals a dismissal by raising one finger

explanation.walkthrough: 'Won't raise a finger' sounds like laziness, but in cricket the raised index finger is the signal that the batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket official raises a forefinger to give a batsman out, so when the batsman survives the finger stays down.

clue.text: C-covering for 20 by 21 down, one may say, not among the 14 acrosses

definitions.text: for 20 by 21 down, one may say, not among the 14 acrosses
definitions.note: a cryptic description of the official's title in sports other than cricket

blocks.note: the letter as printed
hair is a head's covering

explanation.surface: A tangle of cross-references about a cricket umpire and a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is UMPIRE and 21 down CAUGHT, written 'c' on a scorecard. In tennis the umpire is called the chair, a title cricketers do not use.
explanation.definitionFit: The tennis umpire sits on a high seat and is addressed by that seat's name, unlike officials in cricket.

clue.text: Beast saying he feels 23 down inside in a trap

indicators.note: inside puts the exclamation within the beast's letters

blocks.note: a cat is a beast
an exclamation of nausea, 23 down being SICK

explanation.surface: An animal caught in a snare groans that it feels unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in a snare means the animal has been seized and cannot escape.

clue.text: House where Peter, drunk, used to flavour American beer

indicators.note: someone drunk is jumbled and unsteady, so the name's letters are mixed up

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
the letters of the name rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub where Peter got drunk on American beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The hop tree is a North American shrub whose bitter fruit was used as a substitute for hops.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American shrub's bitter seeds served in place of hops for brewing, hence its name.

clue.text: Damage to John, the player

blocks.note: first meaning: harm or injure
second meaning: Sir John ..., the English actor, a player in the theatrical sense

explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests sport, but here it is an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Injury is harm done to someone, and the English film actor John shares the surname.

clue.text: Was fast circulating inside, being unable to solve the clue

indicators.note: circulating means going around, so the hurried word encircles another

blocks.note: sped means went fast
your tum, or stomach, is your inside

explanation.surface: Something rushed around indoors while the solver was stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like the container signal but it supplies letters; 'circulating' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be baffled or at a loss is to be stumped, used of a puzzle that defeats you.

clue.text: Not so well written as it should be to a king

blocks.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark text quoted exactly as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A complaint that a letter to the monarch was badly drafted.
explanation.walkthrough: Sic in brackets tells the reader that an odd spelling is deliberate, copied faithfully from the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone off-colour or nauseous is unwell, the plain sense of being in poor health.

clue.text: Repeat broadcast about 14 across's achievement

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
a cricketer scores runs

explanation.surface: A sports programme shown again about a cricketer's feat.
explanation.definitionFit: A television programme shown a second time is a repeat, the American and British term alike.

clue.text: Composer slightly involved with waterway, being in a drunken revel

indicators.note: only a little bit of the composer gets tangled up in the waterway

blocks.note: J S Bach, the German composer
a canal is an artificial waterway

explanation.surface: A composer is mildly mixed up in a canal, at a drunken party.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of the composer slips one place into the waterway, so the two words overlap rather than simply joining.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Bacchus, Roman god of wine, the word means a wild, drink-fuelled party or orgy.
